title_final: Randomized Trial of Behavior Therapy for Adults With Tourette Syndrome
title_author_manuscript: Randomized Trial of Behavior Therapy for Adults with Tourette’s Disorder
authors: Wilhelm S; Peterson AL; Piacentini J; Woods DW; Deckersbach T; Sukhodolsky DG; Chang S; Liu H; Dziura J; Walkup JT; Scahill L
date_interpretation: Historical 2012 trial; neither later PMC availability nor 2026 extraction is a new publication. Registry study-start month and paper recruitment-start date are different fields. No earlier online publication date inferred.

design.acute: Ten-week, three-site, 1:1 randomized CBIT versus psychoeducation/supportive therapy (PST), allocation stratified within site by tic medication
design.masking: Outcome assessors masked; participants and therapists aware
design.followup: Within-arm, conditioned on acute CGI-I response and returning assessment; not a preserved randomized contrast

population.eligibility: At least age 16, TS or CTD; CGI severity at least 4, YGTSS total tic greater than 14 (greater than 10 for motor/vocal only); English fluency, IQ greater than 80. Co-occurring conditions stable and not requiring other treatment; tic medication stable at least 6 weeks with no planned change.
population.excluded: History of schizophrenia/pervasive developmental disorder; current substance abuse/dependence; four or more prior similar behavioral-treatment sessions
population.applicability: Adult-dominant rather than adult-only; severe/unstable and treatment-experienced patients restricted; not a dedicated persistent-very-severe-adult estimate

interventions.acute: Eight sessions over 10 weeks in each arm; initial two 90 min, subsequent 60 min
interventions.boosters: Three monthly booster sessions specified for acute responders in both arms; treatment section says invited. Actual per-person attendance/completion not supplied in the inspected original report.

counts.flow_source: PMC Figure 1 visually inspected; analyze counts are not inferred by subtracting dropouts

endpoints.primary: Paper design and current registry identify week 10 tic severity; paper Outcomes section also calls YGTSS and CGI-I primary measures. Keep continuous severity and categorical response distinct.
endpoints.response: CGI-I 1 or 2, improvement relative to baseline; no requirement for tic absence
endpoints.continuous_model: At least one postrandomization visit; mixed repeated measures, baseline/site adjusted, missing-at-random assumption; LOCF sensitivity described as same conclusions without numerical estimates

week 10_impairment.status: Secondary in registry, unadjusted multiplicity in paper

endpoints.followup: Original Table 4 gives CGI-I positives with available-case and acute-responder denominators. Direct follow-up impairment and GTS-QOL effects not reported here.
endpoints.quality_of_life: GTS-QOL not identified among original report outcome methods; does not prove no broader functional measures were collected in same trial

adverse_events.ascertainment: Therapist inquiries each session; spontaneous unexpected exacerbation for tic worsening; masked clinician classification at study end
adverse_events.limits: Event counts not unique affected-person counts; no rare-harm or long-term safety exclusion

negative_or_inconclusive_findings: Medication status and initial severity moderator tests were not significant; no equivalence established
Nine of 24 CBIT responders and two of 4 PST responders absent from follow-up
No randomized comparison retained after week 10
No adult-only, withdrawal/off-treatment, direct long-term impairment or GTS-QOL effect identified here

reporting_discrepancies.analysis_choice: 4/59 supported by allocation and body/table; 4/63 conventionally rounds 6.3%

reporting_discrepancies.table: CBIT 12/15 available or 12/24 all acute responders; PST 1/2 available or 1/4 all acute responders
reporting_discrepancies.analysis_choice: Keep denominator categories aligned; no causal selected-arm comparison
Flag arithmetic mismatch; no author calculation or corrected estimate inferred
Final publication where values differ; not an exhaustive diff

funding_conflicts: NIMH grants plus Tourette Syndrome Association support; sponsor role declared absent in design/conduct/analysis/manuscript. Several authors disclosed treatment-manual royalties and professional honoraria; additional disclosures on publisher page.
claim_supported: Acute benefit relative to PST in the analyzed selected trial population; observed CGI-I maintenance among returning acute responders within a booster-inclusive strategy
claim_not_supported: 80% of all randomized participants respond at six months
Tic improvement substitutes for direct quality-of-life or impairment outcomes
correction_retraction_check: Bounded DOI/title searches and PubMed record inspection identified no correction/retraction. Not comprehensive clearance; no historical registry audit.
reviewer: Project NeuroFreedom analysis worker; separate independent computational review

next_verification_task.cohort_overlap: Same NCT00231985 trial, not independent replication
next_verification_task.question: Separate randomized acute effects on disability/social/family functioning from responder-status associations and selected follow-up; verify denominators, instrument-specific direction, uncertainty, multiplicity and null findings before computation
next_verification_task.status: Source identity/relevance verified; full outcome extraction not completed in this task
